(Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) BEIJING, July 29 (Xinhua) -- Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (NPC), met with Slovak President Peter Pellegrini in Beijing on Wednesday. China is willing to work with Slovakia to continuously enhance strategic mutual trust, and deepen high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and cooperation in economy, trade, artificial intelligence and new energy, while promoting people-to-people bonds, Zhao said. He said the NPC stands ready to carry out friendly exchanges with the Slovak National Council in fields such as legislation and supervision, which is expected to better serve the cooperation between the two countries. Pellegrini said that the two countries' adherence to mutual respect, sovereign equality and continuous dialogue has laid a foundation for the long-term and sound development of bilateral relations. Slovakia is willing to enhance exchanges with China to promote understanding, deepen mutual trust and expand cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, he added. https://www.bursa.ro/calin-georgescu-rem.text: The request for the 30-day pre-trial detention of former presidential candidate Călin Georgescu and businessman Ionel Rusen-which had initially been rejected by the judge for rights and liberties at the Bucharest Tribunal-was granted yesterday by the judges of the Bucharest Court of Appeal. The court upheld the appeal filed by DIICOT against the ruling that had previously placed the two men under judicial control; this decision regarding the preventive measure is final, and Călin Georgescu was taken into pre-trial detention last night. This measure was taken after DIICOT placed a judicial lien on Călin Georgescu's home as part of a criminal case in which he allegedly defrauded a businessman from Buzău County. Following the seizure, Georgescu's supporters launched a furious fundraising campaign on TikTok to save their idol's home. As for the criminal case, it stems from financing that a businessman from Buzău, Răzvan Leu, was attempting to secure for a business venture. According to prosecutors, starting in September 2021, three individuals-two Romanian citizens (one of whom is Călin Georgescu) and an Italian citizen-allegedly acted in concert to convince businesspeople that they could facilitate loans from foreign financial institutions. The condition for this was the deposit of financial guarantees. Prosecutors are investigating Georgescu and Rusen for establishing an organized criminal group and for fraud with particularly serious consequences, committed as a continuing offense. In the case reported by Răzvan Leu, the promised financing was initially set at 6 million euros. Investigators allege that, to lend credibility to the operation, the victim was shown loan documentation and procedures, provided with payment account details, and informed of purported approvals. Meetings took place in Romania and the UK, where a loan agreement was allegedly signed. The businessman reportedly transferred over one million euros as a guarantee, but the loan never materialized. Subsequently, according to DIICOT, he was offered an increase in financing to 15 million euros in exchange for an additional guarantee of 100,000 euros. This financing also failed to materialize, and the sums paid were not returned. The financial loss cited by prosecutors exceeds 1.1 million euros. This is the scheme described by the prosecution and remains to be verified during judicial proceedings; the arrest order does not establish the defendants' guilt. On September 21, DIICOT conducted five searches in Bucharest and the localities of Mogoşoaia, Ciolpani, and Buftea. Prosecutors announced the seizure of signal jamming equipment, data storage devices, and identity documents-two passports and an ID card-which are to undergo forensic examination due to suspicions that some may be forged. Călin Georgescu and Ionel Rusen were detained for 24 hours at the time. Three days later, investigators placed a protective seizure on the former candidate's home in Mogoşoaia as part of efforts to recover the alleged financial loss. The Bucharest Tribunal had initially rejected DIICOT's request for pre-trial detention and placed the two men under judicial control. Prosecutors challenged the ruling, and the Bucharest Court of Appeal re-examined the preventive measure yesterday. As the first two judges failed to reach a consensus, the case was resolved by a panel with a casting vote, involving a third magistrate. The court ultimately ordered the pre-trial detention of both defendants. On Monday, Călin Georgescu declared his innocence regarding all three criminal cases against him, claiming they were politically fabricated. It should be noted that the fraud case is still in the criminal investigation stage and, under the law, Georgescu and Rusen benefit from the presumption of innocence. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters Military US Air Force responds to suspected drone activity at RAF Lakenheath No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure at Suffolk site affected, says US military Nadeem Badshah Fri 13 Nov 2026 17.31 EST First published on Fri 13 Nov 2026 16.01 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The US Air Force has said it responded to “suspected unauthorised drone activity” on Friday night at an RAF airbase in the east of England . No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, the air force said. Sirens were heard at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, one of several airbases in the UK used by the US military . The USAF added: “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors and all of our families. “Protecting our shared community is a joint responsibility, and we encourage everyone to support this effort by reporting any unusual or suspicious activity to local authorities.” A UK Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “We are coordinating with all relevant parties regarding reports of unauthorised drone activity at RAF Lakenheath this evening. “USAF security forces personnel responded to the reports and the situation is now resolved. We are working closely with them to establish the facts. We will provide updates in due course.” The MP for West Suffolk , Nick Timothy, said the authorities at the base had told him “there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved”. He added: “Given the raised threat level, I continue to encourage everyone to report anything suspicious or out of the ordinary to the authorities.” RAF Lakenheath said in September it was on “Charlie alert”, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US department of defense. It is home to the 48th fighter wing, also known as the Liberty wing, with almost 7,000 active-duty personnel making it the largest US fighter operation in Europe, according to the official base website. Earlier this year, police investigated an alleged terror plot at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and a trespass incident at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire. Both bases are used by the US Air Force. In the past two months the US has evacuated planes from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk and RAF Fairford in response to suspected attacks on the bases allegedly linked to Iran. Donald Trump said in October that “some threats” led the US to pull its bombers from Fairford. Police said petrol but no explosives were found during searches of vans near the base in Gloucestershire. Two men were charged by the Crown Prosecution Service over their alleged involvement in the incident. This week, at least 12 USAF aircraft departed the nearby RAF Mildenhall base including two Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, with one headed towards Germany and another seen landing at Prestwick airport near Glasgow. Downing Street insisted earlier this week that British airbases are safe and their security is a “top priority”. https://www.dw.com/en/humanitarian-missi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PeoW Prefer DW on Google A Ukrainian soldier from an anti-drone unit patrols a street in Kostiantynivka (January 2026) Image: Diego Herrera Carcedo/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky . According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission. Putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine . Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line. In July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine says the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the main command post of a brigade defending Kostiantynivka in March 2026 Image: Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/AFP Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and said that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city. What is the situation for civilians? Kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk . Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, said Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years. Local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add that Kostiantynivka has no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot. "Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he said. Humanitarian proposals as leverage Kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian issue for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he said, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity. Yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and said the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution. The aftermath of a Russian attack on a residential building in Kostiantynivka in November 2024 Image: Ukrinform/dpa/picture alliance Kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," said Popovych. Ceasefire as military tactic After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky , which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition. Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground. "If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned. Apartment buildings and a church in Kostiantynivka were damaged in Russian attacks in December 2025 Image: National Police of Ukraine/AFP How should Kyiv respond to Moscow's proposal? Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers currently at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested. Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population. The human rights activist said that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said. This article was originally written in Ukrainian.
